name: French Girl
subcategory: 2024 film by James A. Woods and Nicolas Wright
summary: The French Girl is a long-standing aesthetic and cultural trope based on a stereotypical image of a chic, sophisticated, and effortlessly "cool" Parisian woman.
description:
The French Girl is a long-standing aesthetic and cultural trope based on a stereotypical image of a chic, sophisticated, and effortlessly "cool" Parisian woman. Rather than being an accurate depiction of all French women, it is a highly influential popular culture cliché perpetuated by cinema and fashion media. [ 1 ] The aesthetic draws on the concept of nonchalance: a studied carelessness that suggests an innate sense of style without visible effort.

The idealized "French Girl" look is often described as "natural and effortless, achieved with effort." [ 1 ] It involves a minimalist approach to fashion, typically with a neutral color palette, classic garments like trench coats and Breton striped shirts, and simple accessories. Beauty is similarly understated, emphasizing healthy skin, tousled "just-woke-up-like-this" hair, and either a bare face or a single bold element, like red lipstick.

The modern archetype originated in the 1950s and 1960s, heavily influenced by the actresses of French New Wave cinema and the icons of the yé-yé music movement. Figures like Françoise Hardy, Jane Birkin, Jeanne Moreau, and Brigitte Bardot established a look that was both intellectual and alluring, romantic and moody. However, the aesthetic has faced criticism for promoting a narrow and exclusionary standard of beauty that is typically white, thin, and of a specific hair type, failing to represent the diversity of modern France. As noted by critics, the image was largely constructed and popularized by a historically male-dominated media and advertising industry. [ 1 ]
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Effortlessness (nonchalance), natural beauty, intellectualism, confidence, minimalism, romanticism

visualDNA.colour: Neutral palette (black, white, beige, navy), with a pop of red

fashion.Clothes: Berets; Silk scarves; Black bras; Black tights; Striped T-shirts; Vintage or vintage inspired graphic T-shirts; White button-down shirts; Satin slip dresses; Floral print cotton dresses— usually red with white flowers; Leather jackets; Leather skirts; Skinny jeans; Matchstick pants; Loafers
fashion.Makeup and Hair: Red lipstick; Bob haircut; Shoulder length hair with bangs (the key to French Girl hair is that it looks slightly wind-ruffled); Natural makeup or no makeup at all

recipe.technique: Produced by Caramel Films, the film was shot in Quebec City and Montreal. Jean-François Lord served as the cinematographer, with music composed by Scott Price. The film's production design was handled by Jean-André Carrière, and costumes were designed by Mariane Carter.
